name: Seated Twist
intro:
Seated Twist (Ardha Matsyendrasana) is a powerful spinal twisting yoga pose that helps improve flexibility, digestion, and overall body balance. In this posture, the spine is gently rotated, which helps release tension from the back, shoulders, and neck. It also stimulates the abdominal organs, promoting better digestion and detoxification.

This pose is highly beneficial for improving posture and maintaining spinal health, especially for people who sit for long hours. The twisting action massages the internal organs, enhances blood circulation, and helps in relieving stiffness in the lower back.

Regular practice of Seated Twist helps calm the mind and improve focus. It also aids in reducing stress and fatigue while increasing energy levels. This pose is suitable for both beginners and intermediate practitioners when done with proper alignment and breathing.

steps.text: Sit on the mat with your legs extended straight in front of you.
Bend your right knee and place your foot outside the left thigh.
Fold your left leg or keep it straight (as comfortable).
Place your right hand behind you for support.
Exhale and twist your torso to the right.
Place your left elbow outside the right knee for a deeper twist.
Hold the position, breathing deeply, then repeat on the other side.

benefits: Enhances digestion and stimulates abdominal organs
Relieves lower back and neck stiffness
Helps in detoxification of internal organs
Strengthens the back and core muscles
avoid: You have severe back pain or spinal injury
You are suffering from hernia or abdominal issues
You have recently undergone abdominal or spinal surgery
You feel sharp pain during twisting
You are pregnant (consult a doctor before practice)
You have severe hip or knee problems
You experience dizziness while performing the pose
